stem:
Uma knows a straight angle at point $O$ is $180^\circ$. Ray $OP$ cuts it into adjacent angles $\angle AOP$ and $\angle POB$, and $\angle AOP=70^\circ$.

Which claim finds $\angle POB$?

options.text: Call the answer the "whole angle" $180^\circ$, without subtracting the known adjacent part.
Say that finding $\angle POB$ is what creates the straight $180^\circ$ angle at $O$, instead of using the whole to find the unknown part.
The adjacent parts add to the whole: $\angle POB=180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ$.
Report $70^\circ$ as $\angle POB$ only because $70$ is the printed degree number in the stem.

teacher.key_rationale: Adjacent parts of a known whole add to that whole: $180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ$. Naming only the whole, reversing part and whole, or grabbing the printed $70$ all miss that hinge.
